I am a biologist by training and a proteomics data scientist with over six years of experience in clinical and experimental research. I work at the interface of experimental design and data analysis, focusing on mass-spectrometry-based proteomics in protein interaction research, cancer, cardiac disease, and infection biology.

At the University of Freiburg, within SFB1381 - Dynamic Organization of Cellular Protein Machineries and the Laboratory of Protease Degradomics, I build and maintain bioinformatic pipelines for studying protein interactions and proteolytic activity. This includes complexome profiling, co-immunoprecipitation assays, blue-native gel mass spectrometry experiments, and integrative analysis of proteomics, terminomics, lipidomics, and proteogenomics data.

### Recent Collaboration Publications

::: {.card-grid}
::: {.publication-card}
### A single-amino-acid cleavage controls global mitochondrial complex integrity
Quantitative complexome profiling shows how loss of ICP55 processing destabilizes mitochondrial protein assemblies.

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41594-026-01876-7) | [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42675210/)
:::

::: {.publication-card}
### Distinct Assembly Complexes Facilitate cbb~3~-type Cytochrome Oxidase Maturation
Complexome profiling resolves stable assembly intermediates involved in bacterial cytochrome oxidase maturation.

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmb.2026.169945) | [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42447953/)
:::

::: {.publication-card}
### Fractionated proteomics identifies a protein network mitigating resistance exercise-induced damage
Human muscle fractionation, proteomics, and phosphoproteomics reveal a BAG3-linked proteostasis network, supported by a public analysis workflow.

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-75501-y) | [Analysis project](projects/bag3-fractionated-proteomics/)
:::
:::
